ceiling.finding: Metal's recommended working set (115.4GB) is a soft limit. MLX allocated 128GB on a 137GB machine without refusing; the probe stopped at its own 125GB safety cap, not a failure. The real ceiling is ~physical RAM minus OS overhead, not the advertised number.

thermal.machine: 14-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Max 40-core GPU (614 GB/s), 128GB
thermal.finding: On the 14-inch chassis the thermal tax falls on prefill (compute-bound), not decode (bandwidth-bound). 70B-4bit cold vs sustained: decode ~unchanged (13->13 tok/s), but prefill ~2.5x slower hot (98->38 tok/s) and TTFT ~2.4x worse (642ms->1834ms). Independent testing shows the 14-inch drops up to ~25% on sustained GPU load while the 16-inch holds.
thermal.buyer_takeaway: <=32B or bursty/interactive: 14-inch and 16-inch are effectively identical. 70B+ sustained or all-day batch: 16-inch is ~15-25% faster sustained and doesn't degrade mid-session. For always-on inference, a Mac Studio beats any laptop on sustained thermals.

cut_loose.reason: download failed 3x (xet hang, read timeout, connection drop); cut loose. The 4-bit ladder already covers the curve.
